summary.text: 机 is recorded with a wood-related gloss and analyzed as 木 plus sound-bearing 几. Later, the graph was reused for 機, “mechanism,” in a proposed sound-based borrowing; the old tree name and its pronunciation are unknown. (ref003, ref022, ref035)

formation.text: The historical analysis treats 机 as phonosemantic: 木 marks a wood-related category and 几 supplies sound. This analysis concerns the graph recorded with the wood-related gloss, not its later use for 機. (ref003, ref035)

components.text: 木 marks the wood-related category in the historical analysis; the gloss does not identify a particular tree. (ref003, ref029, ref035)
几 is identified as the sound component in the historical analysis of 机. The graph’s reported reading does not establish how the tree word was pronounced. (ref003, ref032, ref035)

sound_limitation.text: The reported historical reading belongs to the graph 机; it does not establish the pronunciation of the tree word or provide an independent sound comparison for that word. (ref032, ref035)

history.text: The selected image is a modern redraw of 機 in small-seal style, not an ancient artifact. It illustrates the recorded analysis of 機 as 木 plus sound-bearing 幾. (ref028, ref034)

Historical accounts record 机 and 機 as separate graphs, with different components and fanqie readings. They describe later use of 机 to write 機 because of similar sound; this established substitution became the simplified form used in mainland China. The first dated occurrence is unresolved. (ref022, ref035)

A phonological dataset gives both graphs the Mandarin reading jī but reports distinct Middle Chinese and Old Chinese forms. The 机 row is local dataset evidence; the upstream source does not independently verify that row. (ref032, ref037)

uncertainties.text: The tree associated with the old wood-related sense and its spoken name are not identified. The graph’s reconstructed reading alone cannot establish the tree word’s pronunciation or demonstrate the proposed sound basis for borrowing 机 to write 機. (ref032, ref035)
Earlier oracle-bone or bronze forms and a graphic development sequence for either graph are not established by the cited material. The selected seal-style image is a modern redraw. (ref026, ref034)
The first dated use of 机 for 機 is unresolved. (ref022, ref035)

senses.text: The historical dictionary glosses 机 as 木也 and analyzes it with 木 and sound-bearing 几. This is the earliest sense supported here, though it does not identify the tree or date an inscription bearing this meaning. (ref003, ref029, ref035)
A phonological dataset associates 机 with “small table” or “stool.” Its date and relation to the wood-related sense are unresolved. (ref032, ref037)
Modern Chinese and Japanese reference data list 机 with the meaning “desk” or “table.” A chronological path from the wood-related or small-table senses is not established. (ref005, ref008)

In mainland simplified writing, 机 is used for the mechanism word written 機 in the traditional graph. This is described as sound-based reuse of a graph, not a meaning change from “wood” or “table”; the old tree name and sound are unverified. (ref022, ref035, ref016)
“Moment” appears among the definitions for 机, but its chronology and whether it belongs to the graph’s independent sense history or its later use for 機 are unresolved. (ref005, ref016, ref035)

developments.text: Both meanings are associated with 机, but no chronology or semantic link between them is established. (ref003, ref032)

Historical accounts describe later writers reusing 机 to write 機 because the words were thought to sound alike. This is borrowing the written sign for a different word, not a shift from “wood” to “mechanism.” Because the old tree name and pronunciation are unknown, the sound match remains proposed rather than demonstrated. (ref022, ref032, ref035)

limitations.text: The earliest date for the wood-related gloss, the tree referent, and its spoken name are unresolved. (ref029, ref033, ref035)
The reported meanings do not establish a secure chronology or connected semantic path among the wood-related, table, desk, and moment senses. (ref005, ref008, ref032, ref037)

overview.text: 机 is recorded for a wood-related meaning: 木 marks that category and 几 supplies sound. Later it was used to write 機, “mechanism,” in a proposed borrowing based on similar sound; the old tree name and its pronunciation are unknown. (ref003, ref022, ref035)

components.text: 木 marks the wood-related category; the particular tree is not identified. (ref003, ref029)
几 is named as the sound component, but its reported reading does not establish the old tree word’s pronunciation. (ref003, ref032, ref035)

takeaway.text: “Mechanism” comes from reusing 机 to write 機 based on a proposed sound similarity, not from a demonstrated change in meaning. (ref022, ref035)

relationships.text: The historical analysis identifies 木 as the meaning component in 机. (ref003, ref035)
The historical analysis identifies 几 as supplying sound in 机. (ref003, ref029)
